## Norfolk Coast National Landscape

The Norfolk Coast National Landscape is a unique landscape covering 453 km2 of rolling chalkland and glacial moraine. It is a setting for nature conservation, farming, recreation, tourism, and industry, but is also a vulnerable coastline, impacted by recreational disturbance, infrastructure developments, and climate change.

The Norfolk Coast National Landscape stretches from The Wash and Sandringham Estate in the West, to Sea Palling and Winterton-On-Sea in the East. It contains one of the highest points in East Anglia (Cromer Ridge at 102 metres above sea-level), National Nature Reserves (e.g. Winterton Dunes, Blakeney Point), and two National Trails (the Peddars Way and Norfolk Coast Path). It is home to approximately 18,280 people and visited annually by approximately 2.8 million people, all of whom enjoy the wild beaches, panoramic seascapes, and diverse wildlife.

Importantly, the Norfolk Coast National Landscape overlaps a number of other nature-based designations, including a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), Special Area of Conservation (SAC), Special Protection Area (SPA), and Ramsar site. These all serve to protect the wildlife and habitats around The Wash and Norfolk coast, which are of national and international importance.

The coastal stretch of the National Landscape is backed by farmland, heathland, wetlands, and woodlands, with buildings and settlements interspersed throughout. Many of these reflect the long history of human management and settlement in the area, and themselves contribute to a special and culturally important landscape; the Norfolk Coast National Landscape is characterised by its historic churches, brick and flint villages, and quay-side towns.

![](https://national-landscapes.transforms.svdcdn.com/production/assets/images/Maps/norfolk_map.png?w=300&auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=crop&dm=1700483317&s=1643b4c5af6bb868b796098cc1f0e4cf)

# Know before you go

Top tips for a fun, safe and memorable experience

## Help us care for our coast

We all have a part to play in protecting our Norfolk Coast, and small actions can make a big difference.

Here are some of the ways you can take action for nature.

![Group of seals on a beach](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2023/10/jemima-whyles-SWl-VmaxYKA-unsplash-scaled.webp)

## Give wildlife space

Our coast is home to an incredible array of species, but they all have one thing in common…they need their space! Be sure to keep your distance from resting birds and seals, steer clear of any cordons and follow any signage. Remember that you are sharing your surroundings with many other creatures – even if you can’t see them!

[Discover our iconic species\\
\\
Discover our iconic species](https://norfolkcoast.org/welcome/iconic-species/)

![](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2025/10/NCPL-Day3-23-scaled.jpg)

## Take the right path

To really escape from it all…please follow the paths! It may be tempting to take a shortcut, but when you move away from the designated route there’s a real risk that you could accidentally trample on delicate vegetation, disturb wildlife or even tread on a well-hidden nest. The same applies for cycling – be sure to keep to marked trails for the best experience.

[Explore our trails\\
\\
Explore our trails](https://norfolkcoast.org/welcome/trails/)

![](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2025/10/NCPL-Day1-98-1-scaled.jpg)

## Leave no trace

We all have a responsibility to care for our coast. Be sure to make use of bins and recycling services, or take rubbish home with you. That includes food waste such as banana skins, which can take up to two years to break down! Our coastal habitats are highly vulnerable to wildfires, so please don’t light fires or BBQs unless you are in a designated area.

![A couple walking their dog through Wiveton Downs](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2023/10/WivetonDowns-Day-30-scaled.webp)

## Follow the canine code

We’re a very dog-friendly coast, and want to make sure you and your pup have the best experience. So check ahead for restrictions, keep your dog under close control, put them on the lead when asked and make sure to clean up after them.

[Visit with your dog\\
\\
Visit with your dog](https://norfolkcoast.org/visitors-with-dogs/)

![](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2026/02/Experience-Burnham-Deepdale-2023-5-10-1-scaled.jpg)

## Keep it green

When we picture our perfect day out on the Norfolk Coast, it doesn’t tend to include queuing for the car park. Why not consider taking the train or bus for your next adventure, or trying out one of our region’s many cycle routes?

[Find out how to get around\\
\\
Find out how to get around](https://norfolkcoast.org/welcome/travel/)

![](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2024/02/Kayaking-BurnhamOvery-35-scaled-1-jpg.webp)

## Plan activities with care

There’s a wide array of adventures on offer in our region, with something to suit all tastes. However, these activities can have an impact on nature, so be sure to choose reputable, sustainable providers to protect wildlife and boost our communities.

## Will you take action for our Norfolk Coast?

By following our guidance during your visit, you’ll be helping to protect this special place, and the species that call it home, for generations to come.

# Walking & cycling

Discover a landscape alive with nature

![Two men walking down a country lane](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2023/10/Experience-Burnham-Deepdale-2023-5-36-1024x683.webp)

## Walking routes

Exploring on foot is one of the best ways to discover the Norfolk Coast.

You can now walk non-stop along the entire Norfolk coastline – although you might like to take a break here and there along the 112-mile route!

We’ve got miles of quiet off-road routes, many of which are accessible for wheelchairs and pushchairs.

Whichever trail you choose, explore at your own pace – take a short walk with friends or head out on a long-distance solo stroll.

See below for links to trails.

![Couple pushing bikes in woodland](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2023/10/Broadland-Cycling-1-28-1024x683.webp)

## Cycling routes

The Norfolk coast is ‘wheely good’ for cycling, whatever your fitness and confidence level.

Bring your own bike on the train or why not think about renting an e-bike for your visit?

We’ve got plenty of shorter or flatter routes for those who like to take it easy. We’ve also got rough stuff for bikepackers, including the Rebellion Way long-distance route.

The Norfolk coast is a cycle-friendly destination. You’ll find lots of places to eat, drink and stay that welcome cyclists, as well as secure parking, toolkits and free water bottle refills at many rest stops.

See below for links to cycle routes.

## Celebrating 40 years

Join us and celebrate the 40th anniversary of the Peddars Way and Norfolk Coast Path.

![](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2025/10/NCPL-Day3-196-scaled.jpg)

## National Trail

Peddars Way (cycling permitted) is a 46-mile route that meets the 112-mile Norfolk Coast Path (cycling not permitted).


[National Trail\\
\\
National Trail](https://norfolkcoast.org/welcome/trails/)

![](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2023/10/Princes-Tower-1-11-scaled.webp)

## Norfolk Trails

Norfolk Trails include a range of long-distance routes and shorter circular walks for walkers, cyclists and horse-riders.

[Norfolk Trails\\
\\
Norfolk Trails](https://www.norfolk.gov.uk/article/42852/Norfolk-Trails)

![](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2024/02/Rebellion-Way-header-jpg.webp)

## Rebellion Way

A challenging 233-mile cycling route, taking you on an off-road adventure through the wilds of Norfolk.

[Rebellion Way\\
\\
Rebellion Way](https://www.cyclinguk.org/rebellion-way)

![](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2023/10/BurnhamOvery-CoastalWalk-22-scaled.webp)

## Travel Norfolk

Use the Travel Norfolk journey planner to plan your walk or bike ride, and connect with local public transport options.

[Travel Norfolk\\
\\
Travel Norfolk](https://www.travelnorfolk.co.uk/)

![A couple walking their dog through Wiveton Downs](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2023/10/WivetonDowns-Day-30-scaled.webp)

## Bringing the dog?

Here are a few simple tips to help you plan your visit with a dog and at the same time help us to protect our wildlife.

[Visitors with dogs\\
\\
Visitors with dogs](https://norfolkcoast.org/visitors-with-dogs/)

![](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2025/06/Walking_and_cycling-key-edited-for-web-resized-1920pxl-wide.png)

## Find your Norfolk experience

[Sheringham Park](https://benorfolk.co.uk/activities/sheringham-park-a-vision-in-a-red-leather-book/)

![Two people walking and one using a mobility scooter in Sheringham Park](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2023/10/1630843-1024x683.webp)

#### Sheringham Park

The park rolls over nearly 1,000 acres of landscaped parkland and wooded glades. Paths meander through magical landscape down to coastal cliffs for glorious year-round exploring.

[Longshore walk](https://benorfolk.co.uk/activities/longshore-walk/)

![](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2023/10/MorstonMarsh_walk-1024x683.webp)

#### Longshore walk

Make time for yourself with this beautiful coastal and marsh walk. Enjoy the sights of the shingle ridge at Cley beach and the orange-billed oystercatchers probing the marshes for shellfish.


[Rebellion Way](https://benorfolk.co.uk/200-mile-cycle-route-launched-in-norfolk/)

![](https://norfolkcoast.org/app/uploads/2024/02/Rebellion-Way-header-1024x867.webp)

#### Rebellion Way

Cyclists up for a challenge will have the chance to tackle Rebellion Way, a brand-new 233-mile route inspired by two of Norfolk’s famous rebel leaders – Boudicca and Robert Kett.

[View more at BeNorfolk.co.uk\\
\\
View more at BeNorfolk.co.uk](https://benorfolk.co.uk/)

[Closer to nature](https://norfolkcoast.org/visit-us/closer-to-nature/ "Closer to nature")

### Longshore walk

Make time for yourself with this beautiful coastal and marsh walk. Enjoy the sights of the shingle ridge at Cley beach and the orange-billed oystercatchers probing the marshes for shellfish.


Rebellion Way



#### Rebellion Way

Cyclists up for a challenge will have the chance to tackle Rebellion Way, a brand-new 233-mile route inspired by two of Norfolk’s famous rebel leaders – Boudicca and Robert Kett.

View more at BeNorfo
We’ve got miles of quiet off-road routes, many of which are accessible for wheelchairs and pushchairs.
Whichever trail you choose, explore at your own pace – take a short walk with friends or head out on a long-distance solo stroll.
Bring your own bike on the train or why not think about renting an e-bike for your visit?

The Norfolk coast is a cycle-friendly destination. You’ll find lots of places to eat, drink and stay that welcome cyclists, as well as secure parking, toolkits and free water bottle refills at many rest stops.
Peddars Way (cycling permitted) is a 46-mile route that meets the 112-mile Norfolk Coast Path (cycling not permitted).
Norfolk Trails include a range of long-distance routes and shorter circular walks for walkers, cyclists and horse-riders.
Use the Travel Norfolk journey planner to plan your walk or bike ride, and connect with local public transport options.
Here are a few simple tips to help you plan your visit with a dog and at the same time help us to protect our wildlife.

approved_stops.name: Winterton Dunes
approved_stops.quote: The Norfolk Coast National Landscape stretches from The Wash and Sandringham Estate in the West, to Sea Palling and Winterton-On-Sea in the East. It contains one of the highest points in East Anglia (Cromer Ridge at 102 metres above sea-level), National Nature Reserves (e.g. Winterton Dunes, Blakeney Point), and two National Trails (the Peddars Way and Norfolk Coast Path). It is home to approximately 18,280 people and visited annually by approximately 2.8 million people, all of whom enjoy the wild beaches, panoramic seascapes, and diverse wildlife.
